title: ccx composer ignores Home and End keys
ccx: Home and End are both no-ops; the inserted characters land at the cursor's existing position -> '❯ abcdef<' then '❯ abcdef<>'
claude: Home jumps to column 0 and End to the line end -> '❯ <abcdef' then '❯ <abcdef>'
suspects: harness/src/tui/ keymap table: no binding for the Home/End escape sequences (ESC[H / ESC[F, ESC[1~ / ESC[4~)

title: ccx composer ignores ctrl+left / ctrl+right word motion (alt+arrows do work)
ccx: ctrl+right does not move the cursor; '1' is inserted at column 0 -> '❯ 1aaa bbb ccc'. ctrl+left is likewise a no-op.
claude: ctrl+right moves one word forward -> '❯ aaa 1bbb ccc'; ctrl+left moves one word back.
suspects: harness/src/tui/ keymap: alt+Left/alt+Right are bound but the ESC[1;5D / ESC[1;5C (ctrl-modified) arrow forms are not

title: word-forward lands in a different place: ccx stops at end of word, claude stops at start of next word
ccx: '❯ one| two three' — emacs forward-word semantics, cursor parks at the end of the current word
claude: '❯ one |two three' — cursor skips the trailing space and parks at the start of the next word

title: Ctrl+C with a draft: claude clears the draft, ccx keeps it and arms exit
ccx: draft is untouched ('❯ draft ZZZ') and the footer gains 'Press Ctrl-C again to exit' — a second ctrl+c quits and the draft is lost
claude: the draft is discarded and the composer falls back to its placeholder ('❯ Try "fix typecheck errors"'); the session stays alive and nothing is armed
suspects: harness/src/tui/ ctrl+c handler — should clear a non-empty composer before arming the exit

title: ccx footer advertises 'Esc clear' but a single Escape does nothing; only two Escapes in a row clear the draft
ccx: one Escape leaves '❯ draft AAA' unchanged even after 3 s, and the next typed character simply appends; two Escapes sent back-to-back do clear it. The footer says 'Esc clear' the whole time.
claude: Escape never clears the draft and claude never claims it does — its footer offers no clear hint (ctrl+c is the clear key, see qa1-04)
suspects: harness/src/tui/ raw-stdin escape disambiguation: a lone ESC appears to be held for a possible CSI prefix and then dropped rather than dispatched on timeout

title: no contextual ghost-text suggestion in ccx's empty composer
repro: run a turn (e.g. 'Count slowly from 1 to 40, one number per line.')
clear the composer and look at the empty composer line
ccx: the composer is bare — only ccx's own reverse-video caret block. The static 'Try "create a util logging.py that..."' placeholder is shown before the first turn and never returns afterwards.
claude: the empty composer carries a dim (SGR 2) contextual suggestion generated from the conversation: 'count from 41 to 80' after the counting turn, 'Never mind, wrong directory' right after an Esc interrupt, 'Try "fix typecheck errors"' on a fresh session. Typing replaces it.

title: ccx hides the hardware cursor and paints its own reverse-video caret; claude moves the real terminal cursor
ccx: cursor_flag=0 and cursor_x=0 in every composer state; the caret is drawn in-band as a reverse-video cell (capture-pane -e shows ESC[7m<space>ESC[0m after the text, and ESC[7m wrapping the character under the caret after alt+b)
claude: cursor_flag=1 and cursor_x tracks the insertion point (8 after 'abcdef', 2 after alt+b; 4 after a single emoji, 6 after adding a CJK char — i.e. correct double-width accounting)
suspects: harness/src/tui/ renderer never emits a cursor-position report and keeps DECTCEM off

title: ccx bash mode renders a doubled '!' sigil in the composer and in recalled history
ccx: '! !echo hi' — the mode sigil is painted and the literal '!' stays in the buffer. Execution is correct (the transcript shows '! echo QA1-BASH-OK' and the real output), so this is display-only. History recall re-renders it the same way: '! !echo QA1-BASH-OK'.
claude: '! echo hi' — the '!' is consumed into the sigil and the buffer holds only the command
suspects: harness/src/tui/ composer prefix rendering: the sigil is prepended without stripping the trigger character from the displayed buffer

title: @ completion: claude offers agents as well as files; ccx offers files only, and lists the tree recursively where claude lists one level
repro: create README.md, src/alpha.ts, src/utils/beta.ts, docs/notes.md in the project
ccx: seven file rows, fully recursive on the first keystroke: '+ README.md', '+ docs/', '+ docs/notes.md', '+ src/', '+ src/alpha.ts', '+ src/utils/', '+ src/utils/beta.ts'
claude: three top-level rows only ('+ docs/', '+ README.md', '+ src/') followed by six agent rows marked with '*': '* claude (agent) – Catch-all for any task…', '* Explore (agent) – …', '* general-purpose (agent) – …', '* Plan (agent) – …', '* statusline-setup (agent) – …', '* claude-code-guide (agent) – …'. Typing 'bet' narrows to '+ src/utils/beta.ts' on both and Tab completes identically.

title: '#' memory mode exists in ccx but has been removed from Claude Code 2.1.222
ccx: '#' switches the composer into a memory mode with the hint '# memory — appends a note to CLAUDE.md (Enter to save)'
claude: no mode change, no hint; submitting sends '# remember: qa note' to the model as an ordinary prompt (spinner 'Warping…', then the model asks what to remember). The '#' prefix is not special in 2.1.222.

title: ccx /history picker draws a 12-column preview pane inside a 118-column box
ccx: the list column is truncated at ~35 columns and the preview is a free-floating 12-column box ('╭──────────╮ │ /history │ ╰──────────╯') starting at column 36, leaving ~70 columns of the picker empty. Frame: docs/parity/qa-findings/frames-qa1/qa1-history-picker-ccx.txt
claude: no equivalent — claude 2.1.222 has no /history command (ccx-only surface), so the comparison is against ccx's own ctrl+r inline search, which is pixel-close to claude's
suspects: harness/src/tui/ history picker layout: preview width is derived from the content instead of the remaining box width

title: ccx never advertises an external editor; claude puts 'ctrl+g to edit in VS Code' on the footer
repro: type a multi-line draft with backslash+return
ccx: footer reads '⏎ send · \⏎ for newline · @ files · / commands · ! bash · ⇧Tab mode' — no external-editor hint anywhere, although ctrl+x ctrl+e does work and round-trips correctly through $EDITOR (vi opened on /tmp/.../ccx-edit-*/PROMPT.md; ' EDITED-IN-VI' came back into the composer)
claude: footer gains 'ctrl+g to edit in VS Code' as soon as the draft is multi-line; ctrl+x ctrl+e also works and, with EDITOR=vi, opens vi on /tmp/claude-501/claude-prompt-*.md and round-trips identically

title: transient composer hints get their own footer line in ccx but are inlined on claude's mode row
repro: press ctrl+u to fill the kill ring, or press ctrl+r to open inline history search
ccx: 'Ctrl+Y to paste deleted text' and 'search prompts:' are each rendered as an extra full-width line above the shortcut row, so the composer block grows and shrinks by a line as you edit
claude: the same strings are appended to the existing mode row, right-aligned or inline ('search prompts: HIST  ⏵⏵ bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle)'), so the footer height never changes

title: ccx picker action hints are lowercase where claude capitalizes the key names
repro: press Esc Esc on an empty composer (rewind picker)
ccx: 'enter to set as default · s to use this session only · esc to cancel' and 'enter to continue · esc to cancel'
claude: 'Enter to set as default · s to use this session only · Esc to cancel' and 'Enter to continue · Esc to cancel'

title: with EDITOR unset, claude's external editor blocks the whole REPL on a GUI editor that may never open; ccx falls back to vi
repro: launch with no EDITOR in env
press ctrl+x ctrl+e (or ctrl+g on claude)
ccx: opens vi in the terminal on /tmp/.../ccx-edit-*/PROMPT.md; :wq returns the edited text to the composer
claude: switches to the alternate screen and shows 'Save and close editor to continue...' waiting on VS Code. In a headless environment nothing ever opens; the only way out is ctrl+c, which exits the whole session in one press ('Resume this session with: claude --resume <id>'). With EDITOR=vi exported, claude opens vi in-terminal and round-trips exactly like ccx.
